title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-11-29
lineage: Transfer: Cassette > Tascam 122 MK3 > Korg MR2000S > DFF @5.6 MHz > Audiogate > wav 24/96. Lineage: wav 24/96 > iZotope RX8 Advanced > wav 16/44.1 > CD Wave > Flac 16
taper: This is Mark Cohen’s tape (Judy Lee’s brother) who worked for Electra records. It was given to Mark by Hail Milgraham, who was a colleague at Electra.

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of a rare 1966 Matrix show packed with early‑Dead rarities (Me & My Uncle, Cold Rain & Snow, Down So Long) – great performance but needs slight pitch correction.
ai_review.review: The set is hailed as one of the year’s best snapshots of ’66, delivering historic performances of Me & My Uncle, The Same Thing and a slew of deep‑cut numbers that deadheads prize. The soundboard source is clear and well‑balanced though it runs a bit slow and requires about +1 % pitch adjustment. Overall the musical energy is high and the rarity factor makes it a standout despite the missing first set.

ai_rating.rationale: The review rates the show 4 ★, praising many rare songs and overall performance while noting minor recording speed/pitch issues; combined weighting yields a strong >4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard mix but runs slightly slow, needs channel swap and about +1 % pitch correction; otherwise an upgrade over previous copies.

standout_songs: I Just Want to Make Love to You
show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set launches with Me & My Uncle and rolls through a string of rarities; third set continues the deep‑cut theme with Down So Long, overseas Stomp, and an eclectic finish. The flow feels like a curated showcase of obscure material rather than a conventional hit‑driven set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia was suffering from a cold and stepped back from vocals, asking Phil to sing; his guitar work is still noted as solid on tracks like Cold Rain & Snow.
band_member_comments.Phil: Called upon to handle vocals due to Jerry’s cold, but no specific comment on bass playing.
